content: Magnesium gluconate is prescribed to treat low levels of magnesium in the blood. This condition can result from gastrointestinal disorders, prolonged vomiting or diarrhea, kidney disease, or other medical conditions. Certain medications can also lower magnesium levels. In some cases, magnesium gluconate may be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Magnesium gluconate is available in tablet and liquid forms for oral administration. It is typically taken two to four times daily, depending on your specific condition. Follow the instructions on your prescription or package label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take magnesium gluconate exactly as directed. Do not take more or less than prescribed, and do not take it more frequently than instructed. To minimize side effects, take this medication with meals. If you are using an extended-release product, do not chew or crush the tablet. Some tablets may be crushed and mixed with food, but confirm this with your doctor or pharmacist. Before taking magnesium gluconate, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to magnesium gluconate or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially other magnesium-containing products, tetracycline antibiotics (e.g., Achromycin V, Panmycin, Sumycin), digoxin (Lanoxin), nitrofurantoin (Furadantin, Macrobid, Macrodantin), penicillamine (Cuprimine, Depen Titratable), and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of kidney disease, stomach problems, or intestinal disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking magnesium gluconate, contact your doctor immediately. A balanced diet typically provides sufficient magnesium. However, supplements may be necessary in cases of illness or medication use. Magnesium is found in various foods, including green leafy vegetables, nuts, peas, beans, and cereal grains with intact outer layers. A high-fat diet may reduce magnesium absorption, and overcooking food can also decrease magnesium content. Follow the dietary recommendations provided by your doctor or dietitian. If you are unsure whether you are getting enough vitamins and minerals, consult your healthcare provider. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Magnesium gluconate may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience diarrhea or stomach upset, especially if these symptoms are severe or persistent. Serious side effects, such as stomach cramps, vomiting, flushing of the skin, or dizziness, require immediate medical attention. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor may order lab tests to monitor your response to magnesium gluconate. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
